title: The dark years
hook: after King Langdarma, monasteries were closed and the teaching went quiet

segments.voice: Yesterday: the debate at Samye, sudden awakening against step by step. Your line: gradual and sudden.

A few monks lead pack animals east, away from central Tibet. In the loads are books of the monastic rules. Behind them, the Tibetan histories say, King Langdarma has turned against the monasteries, and the halls that earlier kings built and filled are emptying. The monks aren't carrying gold. They're carrying the rules for how a monk is made, so that one day it can be done again. And the question rides with them: what keeps a practice alive when there's nowhere left to practice it in the open?
screen: `MONKS HEAD EAST.` → `THE RULES IN THEIR PACKS.` → `WHAT KEEPS A PRACTICE ALIVE?`

segments.voice: The histories tell it sharply. Langdarma turns against the monasteries, and the royal support they lived on is cut off. His reign ends violently, and after it the old empire breaks apart among rival lords. For a long stretch there is no king to invite an abbot and no royal temple to pay for. Historians today ask whether Langdarma was as fierce as the later accounts say, or whether the loss of royal money did much of the damage on its own. Either way, the great monasteries went dark. But quiet isn't the same as gone. The stories remember three kinds of keepers. A few monks who fled to the far east of Tibet with the monastic rules, so the line of ordination could one day be handed on again. Lay practitioners, married men and women in villages, who kept chanting and meditating at home, out of sight. And the texts themselves: scrolls hidden away and, in the Nyingma telling, teachings Padmasambhava had concealed to be found when the time was right. Those hidden teachings are called terma, treasures. That's what a hard time looks like from inside a tradition. Mostly not a grand stand. A rule remembered. A chant said low in a kitchen. A scroll wrapped and set aside. Small things kept going, because nobody knew when the doors would open again.
screen: `THE MONASTERIES GO DARK.` · `MONKS CARRY THE RULES EAST.` · `VILLAGERS KEEP IT AT HOME.` · `TEXTS HIDDEN AS TREASURES.` · then, large: `IT WENT QUIET.`

segments.voice: Choose one small thing you could do even on your worst day, a few slow breaths, a line you say, one kind act, a moment of thanks, small enough that nothing could stop you. Do it now, quietly, as if no one would ever know, and let the rest of the sit be that one practice, kept.
Terma. Hidden treasures, texts and teachings concealed to be found later, kept safe through Tibet's dark years after King Langdarma.
Your line: it went quiet. Small things, kept, carried it through. Day nine hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Tibetan Buddhists tell the story of the dark years as a lesson in endurance, and the Nyingma tradition honors treasure revealers who bring to light teachings said to have been hidden by Padmasambhava.

chat.says: When Tibet's monasteries closed, how did the teaching keep going?
options: Monks carried the rules east, villagers practiced at home, texts were hidden.
It didn't; everything was lost, and Tibet had to start over from nothing.
The king who closed them secretly kept them running inside his palace.
chat.meaning: The stories remember three keepers: monks carrying the rules east, lay practitioners at home, and hidden texts, called terma in the Nyingma telling.

Langdarma.meaning: the king the histories say turned against the monasteries

terma.meaning: hidden treasures: teachings concealed to be found later

Nyingma.meaning: the old school of Tibetan Buddhism

Padmasambhava.meaning: Guru Rinpoche, who, the Nyingma say, concealed teachings

notes: Claims rule: no dates; the traditional 'three monks' who fled to Amdo given as 'a few monks'.
Langdarma's assassination (by the monk Lhalung Palgyi Dorje in the traditional account) summarized as 'his reign ends violently'; confirm this restraint is appropriate.
Historians' revision (that the persecution may be exaggerated and loss of royal patronage decisive) put briefly and fairly; confirm.
Terma glossed as 'treasures'; confirm, and that linking terma to this period is presented as the Nyingma telling.
Myth item 2 uses 'all agree' only as a false statement; it makes no claim about scholars.
